utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: January 15th, '93. Around January 15th or 19th, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to being able to leave, did you need some assistance from Mr. Kupresanin in getting documents in order to leave?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in view of the fact what the International Red Cross agreed to assist, assist me in leaving this area, they asked that some kind of a personal ID of mine would be given to the Red Cross. Since I really didn't have any ID, and they couldn't put me on the list of persons without any kind of ID, the only thing that could be done was to obtain some kind of document from the police in Banja Luka or any other kind of authorities. And then the Red Cross contacted them. And then my sister had to go into the municipality and ask that some kind of ID be issued to me. They said it was not possible to do so and then one day later, a person from Banja Luka who was friendly with Kupresanin and had a conversation with him and said they would give me some kind of ID --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, is this going to assist us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us have a copy of it then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit 43.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, do you recognise Exhibit 43?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it's that certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the certificate, who gave you the certificate?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That certificate was issued by Vojo Kupresanin it was issued to his friend and then this friend, in turn, delivered it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How does Mr. Kupresanin refer to Omarska in the last page of that document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He calls it a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That's all we have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is that your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Vucicevic, do you want to make a start now or do you want to break before you -- you would like the break? Very well, quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: May it please the Court?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, my name is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, your questions in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I thought -- Cross-examined by Mr. Vucicevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, my name is Mr. Vucicevic, and I represent Dr. Milan Kovacevic in these proceedings. We have heard that you suffered a lot for the period that you testified and I personally regret what happened to you. I know how difficult it must be for you to recall and go through all of these events, but I will have to go -- just as a part of my professional duty as an attorney, is to go and examine you about some of these details. And, Your Honours, I do thank you for your latitude for allowing me to give a little introduction. Mr. Semenovic, you said in your testimony you were born in the Village of Srpska near Vlasenica. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's a village called Srpska, in Municipality of Vlasenica, in the eastern part of Bosnia. I was only born there and my parents moved in 1964 into the Prijedor Municipality. And from the age two I have been living in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that your parents moved to the Prijedor Municipality, is that in the city of Prijedor itself or any of the villages or hamlets?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First they moved into the village of Rizvanovici in the village of Prijedor. And that's where we lived for about seven years. And, after that, my father got the job in Kozarac in the village of Brdjani and then we moved into Brdjani and spent the next years there. After that, my father got a job in Trnopolje and then we lived in Trnopolje up until the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you finish high school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: High school Esad Midzic in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go the Tuzla to study mining immediately after finishing your high school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, first I went into the army. I served the mandatory army service that every healthy male had to serve. And then, after the army service, I went to the university in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military in the town of Leskovac, Republic of Serbia, did you spend all of your time in Leskovac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that you were assigned to the artillery unit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what was your rank?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't have a rank. Towards the end of my military service, I was a private, but it wasn't a high, high-ranking position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you assigned to the artillery unit from the very beginning or there was some boot camp or preparatory training for the service?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the JNA, all the young men who joined the army who go on to the military service, they all go through the training that lasts for several months. And then after the training is completed, they are stationed in the barracks and the training really specialises privates for certain duties in the Yugoslavia National Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were prepared as a specialist for the artillery unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was just a plain soldier in the artillery. I wasn't a specialist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties as the private soldier in the artillery unit? As you said, you were not a specialist then.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was a private soldier, so I did not have any commanding authorities. My -- I was part of the crew in the Howitzer of one of 5 millimetres. They had a person who was targeting and then they had the other crew members that were providing the ammunition. I was part of this crew for a while. And then, I was for a while, I was a gunner on the Howitzer 105 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long -- strike it. Have you performed all of these duties in your unit that you have just described?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Every soldier did that because all of the privates had to go through certain stages, you know, learning how to use the weapons. You know, everybody had to go through the training and gunning and in placing the Howitzers. And then, towards the end, each would be assigned a certain role. And then when we had training, we knew well in advance who would have what role, who would be the gunner, who would be putting in the ammunition and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long of a time span did you spend as the fellow who was bringing the ammunition to the gun? Or how much time did you spend as the soldier who was charging up the gun and how much time did you spend as the aiming soldier?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just like any other soldier, the training was set up in such a way so that each soldier in the artillery had to learn all of these operations. And then at the end of the training, you would get a military speciality and I was the gunner. This duty was awarded to me at the end of the training, through which all of the privates that are member of the artillery units go through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to get this certificate that you are an aiming soldier on the gun, how much training did you have to have and what was the scope of your training?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The training covered all basic military aspects, the aiming, the targeting, what to do in case of nuclear attack, nuclear explosions, how to take positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers were in the basic artillery units?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean my unit? In Howitzer unit -- no, platoon is a larger unit. The elementary one is a crew of five persons that serve the Howitzer one of five. And larger calibres have larger crews, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the rank of the commanding officer of the few Howitzers that were comprising one unit? What was the rank of the officer who was commanding you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the captain that was your training officer at that time or commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: His nickname was Djuro, I don't remember his name. I served in the army in 1982.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of any other lower ranking commanders in your unit besides captain?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the Corporal Kovac. I remember some of the nicknames, but not the names because it was a mixed nationality situation. There were Macedonians, Slovenians --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides doing your regular duty, camaraderie, friends, staying together after the official hours of exercise have passed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you haven't made any friends at all, you just spent all the time in the army for two years just by yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The military service was one year long, not two. And, of course, during the service, we have made friends, which is normal. But I have already mentioned that the people where from Macedonia, Slovenia, Serbia, and later I didn't travel to Slovenia for many years and neither did I travel to Macedonia, so most of these people I've never met them again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking, Mr. Semenovic, maybe you're not getting my question correctly, have you made any friends with these young men, regardless of what former part of Yugoslavia they were, just at that time, did you make any friends, not whether or not you maintained the friendship throughout the years later?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, all of us in the unit, we were all friendly with each other. We had, after the training, we had certain spare time and, of course, after that, we did socialise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You slept in the same bedroom, big bedrooms. How many soldiers slept in that bedroom together?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Somewhere about fifteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you and your fellow soldiers also ate in the same cafeteria, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was a central cafeteria for the barracks and all the soldiers ate there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of you ate the same food, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, everybody was offered the same food. People ate what they liked and some people -- people ate what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard any jokes, at that time, for any of the soldiers refusing to eat certain foods?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know for myself, I did not see what other people, I was not interested in what other people ate or did not eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody joke because -- strike it. Have you refused to eat certain foods at that time that were offered to you as a part of the regular meals?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I ate what I wanted to eat from the food that was offered to me. And those things I did not want to eat, I just left them. If I didn't like the food that was prepared, I would only eat the first meal, the appetiser and some fruit and that was enough for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certain foods on religious grounds?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of your fellow soldiers make fun of you or make any jokes because you practice your religion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a religious man, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And making mockery of somebody's religion, or religious practice is indeed a serious matter to the true believer, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll move on to the next line of questioning. You said that when you came back from the military, you enrolled to the university in Tuzla. Have you obtained a degree, an engineering degree from mining from the University of Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me, what were the employment that you held later on from the time that you graduated through beginning or middle of '89?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After I graduated, actually after I had listened to all the courses, but before I graduated, my father died and I had to start working in order to feed my family because my sister studied at the same time and we planned that she should graduate first and then she should get a job, which would allow me to graduate. For about a year, I was employed by a private employer. I actually worked with my friends, we processed wood, timber, and we sold the products that we manufactured. At the same time I studied and I also passed all the exams that I had to and I was writing my thesis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you graduate soon thereafter or -- and obtain some other job, that is, that you were professionally qualified for?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I graduated later. I had this job and that is how I -- I graduated later in '95. I had passed all the exams, but the events that we have been discussing here took place, so I defended my thesis formerly in '95.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so I would have the time perspective here, when did you finish your prescribed courses, as you said, what year was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had any other jobs throughout '88 and '89?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was not employed by the state. I stress again, I studied at home and passed my exams and, at the same time, I worked, because I had to support my family and my sister who was at the university at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All what I am trying to find out, when did you get into the university, when did you get the first job and what other jobs you had. If you could just try to put it to me as plainly as possible. Because I am not trying to make it difficult. I am just trying to find out, what were your life experiences?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Having served in the national service, I finished that in 1983, so after 1983, I studied in Tuzla. I attended -- I finished attending all the courses in '88.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had any state jobs after finishing the university besides that private enterprise, small business that you worked for?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a state positions, state jobs, have you held?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had several jobs in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that something that you have done after these events of 1992? I am not looking into what he has done after 1992, I am just looking before all these events happened. I just want to limit this.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the period before 1992, I held the position in the parliament. And pursuant to a decision of the parliament, I was made into a professional. I gained a professional status. It was in the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you received by the decree of the parliament?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That the function of the member of the parliament is a -- has a professional status because the law enabled us to do so. There were certain members of the parliament, who were there as professionals. That means that they were paid for the job that they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any members of the parliament that were not declared as professional men that did some other jobs and were doing their political duties as the members of the parliament part-time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am bringing you now to the second half of 1989. You testified that in Tadic's case that you participated, and I am directing, Your Honours, if it would be any help, page 892, and it's line 4. I participated in the foundation of the Party of Democratic Action. Could you tell me, how did you get an idea to pursue this political activities? Was it your own or somebody suggested to you, Mr. Semenovic, let's proceed with this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was my idea. And I joined these activities in 1990 and not in 1989 as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, tell me, how did you get keyed in, as I am using your term, or came on board. Your Honours, I am listening to the witness and getting, you know, the questioning I am not looking at the -- maybe I should -- how was it translated, so I can help you exactly you know, with terminology. Well, how did it come about that you began to participate in the political activities?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wanted to join the process, which I saw as an opportunity for the democracy to come to this area where we lived because we had watched these processes take place in the neighbouring countries.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please wait until the end of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you get together in order to start the political cell in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sorry, to interrupt, Your Honour, there is a request from the translators to allow the translator to finish with the answer before the counsel begins again. It would be helpful for you to wear the headphones and then you can hear when they're done because it is difficult. We don't get the answer, the full answer, because he talks over and they have to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll pause, with the headphones, I feel a little restricted when I am on my feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, all what I am trying to find out, a few friends, a few associates that you got together and in starting a political movement that you just, whose goals you just described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What was the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, all what I am trying to find out, who are the few friends and few associates that you got together and started a political movement with the goals that you just described? Who are those friends? Who are those individuals?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These were my friends who shared the same ideas with me in the Municipality of Prijedor. When we saw that parties were being formed, we decided to join in in the process. And we formed the steering committee for the formation of the SDA in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Initiating committee of the SDA in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was myself, Nijaz Kapetanovic, Dr. Iljas Music, Becir Medunjanin, Islam Bahonjic, Husein Bahonic, Jusuf Delkic, Hamid Saftic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you met for the first time and established the initiating committee?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We met for the first time and discussed this topic in a cafe in Prijedor. We called it Dzavidova Cafe. It's an old Bosnian cafe. This is the first time when we discussed this idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when was it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was in July, 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you decide then and how did you follow on your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The programme of the SDA was acceptable to us, we were able to read about it in the papers. We decided that one of us should travel to Sarajevo and to ask for the materials from a representative of that newly formed parties so that we can study the materials. And if we realise that they were in agreement with our ideas, that we should join the party and form a branch office of that party in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (No microphone).

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was in the second half of May. In early June it was registered. I think it was registered in the first half of June in 1990. I can't recall the exact date, but I think it was thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who were the founding officers of the SDA in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew about some of them and for others I did not know. I remember some names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (Microphone not on).

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, he was one of the founders. Savet Isovic, he was a singer, a well-known person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you remember of?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some other persons whose names I learned from the press, from the media, and I did not know a lot about them beforehand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read anywhere about the programme of this newly established SDA from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The programme was everything that you testified yesterday, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last day when you were in court.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few days ago, on Wednesday, you were here testifying for the Prosecutor's case in chief and Mr. Keegan was asking you about the programme of the SDA and now I am asking you, did you say and stated everything that you knew about SDA programme at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: What time are you referring to? What period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May, June of '90, about the programme of the SDA at that time. Or, perhaps, your testimony referred to some other programme or some other time.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that portion of my testimony did refer to the programme, to the basic elements, but the programme of the party was very broad. And you could talk about it for a long time. Something else too, the basic guidelines of the parties, of most of the parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina were practically the same, market economy, human rights, full national and religious freedom, freedom of the press and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when was the SDS established in Prijedor established and where?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was founded in the end of August or beginning of September. And the constituting assembly was held in the sports hall in Prijedor. And I was there at the constituting or founding assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, your testimony is that the SDS was formed a few months after SDS -- after SDA was formed in Prijedor; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, SDA in Prijedor was founded on the 17th of August and you asked me when it was founded in Sarajevo. As I said, in Sarajevo, it was founded in June. That is when it was officially registered. The steering committee of the party of the SDA party in Prijedor was formed, as I have already said, in July. But the facts of the founding -- but legally speaking, it's the moment when the founding assembly was held and that was in August. In a brief period, both the SDS and the SDA were established in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just stated a few minutes ago that you were present at the founding assembly of the SDS in Prijedor; am I correct on that one?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No -- yes, that's correct, I was present at the founding assembly, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you invited to that founding assembly by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who invited you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The collective leadership of the Party of Democratic Action was invited. The main officials of the party, the SDS invited the SDA and that's how we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: SDA was formed before SDS in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it is shortly before SDS, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You observed the founding assembly of SDS in Prijedor, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their goals were freedom of the press, privatisation of the economy, freedom of religious expression, human rights, just as were the goals of SDA; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they declared in public. These were their public positions that they took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you found them, you, yourself, you found them and, indeed, a natural ally to overturn the communist government which was in power for proceeding 45 years; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have cooperated with the SDS officers in the pre-election campaign?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified, the only time that you saw the accused was at the meeting where the poster was discussed; isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the first time that I saw him. That was not the only time, however.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that meeting, could you just remind me, where was the meeting held?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the new hotel in Prijedor, upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it -- to the best of my recollection, there is a big dining hall on the floor on the Prijedor hotel; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was to the left of that hall. When you look from the beginning of the hall where the band played, to the left there is a corridor and there are offices there in that corridor. The doors of that corridor are to the left, the first, second, third door. And the meeting was held in the first office to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the meeting, was Dr. Kovacevic already present in that room?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because they had a meeting of their own before that. That's what it had seemed to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of -- how many men were in that room before you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ten to twelve men, I think there were twelve of them. At any rate, there were many and we had expected only two of them to be there. I think there were ten or twelve of them because the whole side of the table, it was a long table, it was full of people. It was a table where people could sit on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were expecting to see only two representatives from the SDS; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the arrangement was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the new hotel in Prijedor is basically the biggest hotel in Prijedor, right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people, when they go out, quite often go to new hotel in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some people went to the new hotel, some people went somewhere else, wherever they wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the discussion about the poster, my client, Dr. Kovacevic, has made the remarks that the name "Yugoslavia" should be on the poster; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it true that, at that time, Yugoslavia was an official country, intact country and country of which all of you were the citizens?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but we were now preparing for the elections in the Republic, not at the federal level. These were the elections for the authorities of the Republic and the poster had to do with the elections for the Republic, not for the federal level, for the area of all of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Yugoslavia had principles of equality of nations up to that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but it had nothing to do with the poster. We had the republic elections, some republics had already conducted the elections. And then the election in Bosnia followed. We were making the poster for the pre-election campaign in the Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not results of the elections in the other states, but what was happening at that time when you were preparing for the election in Bosnia? Since Dr. Kovacevic insisted that the word "Yugoslavia" would be enclosed, indeed, that could reasonably assume that he was concerned about equality of the nations. The principle that you just said existed in Yugoslavia, just one of the reasonable conclusions. Is it possible to conclude that? There might be some other conclusions, but that's one of the conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We understood that and we put the word "Yugoslavia" on the poster and we accepted the position of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, this coalition between SDA and SDS was indeed so strong, that there was an agreement made ahead of the election how to divide the power in the case of victory; isn't it correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, on the level of the leadership of the party leadership, there was an agreement. I am not quite certain as to the content of the agreement, but immediately after the elections, the principles of the allocation of power were defined in a written form and the parties even have a written agreement on the percentage of allocation of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to win the election in Bosnia at that time, one party, as I understood the government, one party must have more than 50 per cent of the aldermen on the municipal level; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They had to have over 50 per cent of the votes in order to create the government on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, therefore, it is unfair to state that SDA won elections in Prijedor, is it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it is not unfair. It is a correct statement in accordance with the election law that was in force at that time, the party who took most of the votes won the election. If it happened to be 20 per cent and all other parties, and there were a lot of them had 5 per cent, then the party that got 20 per cent of the vote was the winning one. So the party, as I said, was the majority of the percentage of votes. The other problem is that with only 20 per cent of the votes, that party could not create a government on its own. That's a separate issue. But, as the law regulates, only the party with more than 50 per cent of the votes can create a government on its on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And testify on the accuracy or anachronism on the sum of the laws that existed in the communist Yugoslavia, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am sorry to interrupt, but it's happened about four or five other occasions, where Mr. Vucicevic is beginning his questions again before the translation of the answer has finished and we have been unable to get complete answers from the witness in translation. So I would just appeal if you would at least either put on the headphones or watch the screen more carefully, so we can get complete answers before the next question begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I will try to observe the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The election law was quite clear, there was no an anachronism or confusion in the law itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, the leadership of your party could have made a deal with, with the other parties besides the SDS and achieve the electoral victory, but found them unsuitable. Why were those parties unsuitable for coalition for the officials of your party?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We didn't want to enter the coalition with the Communist Alliance and all the other parties that emerged from the alliance of communists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will proceed now, after the election. The elections were held and the main responsibility of the parties was to form the municipal government. You testified there was no difficulties in selecting the mayor, the deputy mayor, the president of the executive board; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the executive board, two of them. All of these positions--

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --had to be confirmed because those mayor and deputy mayor are elected positions, they were elected as the aldermen and then elected by their constituents, but all of these positions had to be confirmed by the municipal assembly; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of these officers were confirmed by the unanimous votes of the coalition alderman?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't recall if the election was unanimous, but the assembly did confirm the president that were elected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a guest, perhaps, at the inaugural assembly or the founding assembly of the first three municipal assembly in Prijedor, perhaps could have been in order?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing a single SDA alderman voting against the slate for the officers?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't recall --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present as a guest in the first row and I didn't look back to see who was voting and who isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the votes officially posted or announced by the presiding officer?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will move on to the distribution of power. And you said that the difficulties arose with the appointment of the chief of police; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that as an example, as a very good example, and this arose with respect to several positions, not just the position of the chief of police, but this issue itself was the most obvious with respect to the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the procedure at that time by which the head of police is being appointed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The chief of police at that time after the coordination concerning the candidates among the political parties, the chief of police was appointed by a formal decree of the Minister of Internal Affairs, if I remember correctly, but only after the coordination among the parties concerning the candidates and confirmation that they are in agreement concerning the candidates in accordance with the allocation of power among the parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The electoral victory, you have testified that you promised to your voters, to your supporters if you win that you should appoint a head of police; isn't that correct? You testified to that fact?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stated that as one of the examples of the pre-election promises, and there were many pre-election promises, just like in every campaign, but people expected that because for decades they didn't have an opportunity to see a Bosniak, a Muslim on that post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have testified, and I will specify the language, tomorrow the line and the page, but you have testified and used the word, therefore, 45 years, the heads of police have been Serbs. To my previous answer, you said there was no Bosniak Muslims, but you have said that those were Serbs, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, I said -- I stated what I knew based on the information that I had. Of course, I was born in 1962 and I have been living in Prijedor since 1964. I don't know what happened in the 40s and in the 50s, but from what I heard from the elderly and from the time when I was born and I was aware, I know that it was always the Serbs that held that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pre-electoral campaign, you have spoken about Serbs having this power position for 45 years, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't give that example. We never used those terms during the pre-election campaigns. In fact, we didn't analyse that from the nationalistic example. We sincerely wanted to go beyond that communist stage and to enter the democratic society that we have witnessed in the countries around us. People travelled and they know that in other countries, people live better, they have more freedom in the democratic countries. And that's just what we wanted. We wanted to seize the monopoly of one party of the league of communists. And always during the pre-election campaign, this is what we stated because that is exactly what our intention was. We didn't specify what nationalities had what posts. Simply, that wasn't what we cared about at that time. We had the same view, the same position towards Bosniak and Serbs, we simply made a distinction based on what position people held. And we wanted the people to be free to elect their own parties, their own people, and to follow the programmes that they wished to follow and to establish the government on this democratic principle where there just wouldn't be one party, but multiple parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, indeed, if one takes what you just said on its face value, it wouldn't have made any difference whether the chief of police was Serb, Muslim, Serb communist who declared themselves a Yugoslav or a Muslim who didn't practice and declared him Yugoslav, it really wouldn't matter, would it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It would matter and for the following reasons: The factual situation in Prijedor Municipality during the communist regime was such that it was mostly the Serbs that held high positions. For example, Prijedor, I think, had 19 public companies. And in 18 leading managing positions -- in 18 companies --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the political appointee, you're going into the economy. I mean, if you can stay on this one, on the political appointee and the chief of police. If you could answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is exactly what I am talking about. I wished to say the following: People understood, realised, that if we gained the opportunity to have the multiple party, democratic system, then in the national respect, the power will be balanced, allocated in a balanced way. There wouldn't be a situation where we would have 18 Serbs on leading positions and only one Bosniak and this is the issue that we raised during the pre-election campaign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you find somebody to be a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We know based on their name and last name. There is a clear distinction there. And also, whether they're religious, we know whether they go to the church or to the mosque and also people in certain situations state openly their views.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Basically, I would like to narrow this question a bit more. Is a Serb being born into the religion an ethnicity, or there is some other requirements or criteria?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I am a Bosniak, a Muslim, and I know that I was born as such. What you asked, I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that -- does definition, a Serb, include a man who was born with a Serbian first name and last name, but who doesn't practice Orthodox religion, is that a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For me, a Serb is a person that states openly that he or she is a Serb. We in Bosnia make this distinction among ethnic background very well. It's a matter of personal choice. They were people who were -- who were of a certain nationality, but they stated that they were Yugoslavs. And, among Yugoslavs, the majority, at least this is what the statistics showed, the majority of Yugoslavs were Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it perhaps be that any of the police chiefs in Prijedor in 50 years prior to your electoral victory, could it be that it was some of those, perhaps that were denoted as Serbs, they were Yugoslavs?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The nationality, Yugoslav nationality, was introduced relatively late. Immediately after the Second World War, after the communists took over, the law prescribed that they were officially only Serbs, Croats and Bosniak Muslims could either declare themselves as Serbs or as Croats and later on they were given the opportunity to declare themselves as undecided. At that time, we didn't really have Yugoslavs. From what I know, this declaration of being a Yugoslav was introduced only in the 70s. I am not quite sure of this, but I think that this term was not used in the constitution prior to that, the Yugoslav nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, in your high school report notes, and so were in mine and generations before us, were categories "nationality," and they were one printed Yugoslavian and another dash line for everybody else to write, wasn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was that line there, that item where you could enter your nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether there was a Yugoslav written therein?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So perhaps some of these police chiefs could have been Yugoslavs, so you don't know definitely that they were Serbs, do you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already explained that term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Semenovic, the police chiefs, as you said, was the first power position that the coalition partners stumbled upon in Prijedor, that's true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: One of the problems was also the post of the police chief in the allocation of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the native language, you used the word "power," you didn't use "political appointees," you did not use "functionaries," you didn't use anything else and you repeatedly used the word "power"; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The power means the carrying out of certain functions in the municipality, in the government service. In our Bosnian language that means to have the power -- to exercise power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you ran for the political office, you ran to get the power, but not to serve the people, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think that's going to be a very helpful line of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were travelling with Dr. Srdo Srdic quite often to Sarajevo. He was a Serbian representative into the council of citizens; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Not -- I didn't travel often with him. I travelled several times, but not often. However, we were together on the parliament sessions and I saw him frequently there. Because I mostly took the train into Sarajevo and to sessions and Srdic generally travelled in a luxury car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified last Wednesday that SDA had finally obtained their man as the police chief in Prijedor and that was upon the assistance of the political tops from Sarajevo, SDA and SDS; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and after that, the leadership of SDS and SDA agreed and Prijedor, to divide these posts in such a way. So there was an agreement between the leaders of SDA and SDS in Prijedor and after which an allocation was achieved. But I did say that this was done only after the intervention, after the urging from the leaders on the republic level, as far as I remember, because I was not a participant in these discussions. But I know that this was the only way to solve the problem because SDS did not agree at the local level to completion of the allocation of power in this manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a member of the parliament and quite often in touch with the political leadership in Sarajevo, somebody has informed you about what you just testified; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, I insisted, since we were unable to agree at the municipal level, since the SDS refused to honour the agreement on the allocation of power that had already been achieved, that we should address the leadership in Sarajevo. And the Prijedor SDS refused that suggestion. In the end, they agreed that these consultations should be carried out at the republican level and allegedly Kadiric said, let them put their man on that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who informed you of this statement of Dr. Kadiric?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the parliament, I was able to see Srdic consult Kadiric on such matters. And the SDS leadership in Prijedor formally agreed, they said, "All right, the agreement has been achieved. You have the post of the chief of police."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's reasonable to conclude that the officials of SDS in Prijedor disregarded at times, directions and orders from the political top; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They did not reject the instructions, they carried them out, just as they did when they agreed that the SDA should have the key function of the chief of police, but only after the intervention of the central office of SDS in Sarajevo. That's when the municipal leadership accepted that and honoured it after that. Before that, they refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last Wednesday you testified, there was an exhibit introduced, about power sharing between the SDA and the SDS and that was passed on the SDS in Prijedor, therefore, it seems that looked like a directive, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These are the principles. The percentages and general functions are indicated there. If a party wins a certain percentage of votes, it gets the post of the president, the second party, the runner up has the post of vice president. Then you have chief of departments, deputies and so forth. This is what is indicated in that document. You don't have the definition of specific posts that one party should get the post of the chief of police and the other the post of the president of the executive board. You have just the generalist terms there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, that was the first government, I think it was Mr. Deli Mustafic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the gentleman personally?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know him personally, intimately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One politician --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, as a member of parliament, I saw him in the parliament. Sometimes he would submit reports and that's how I know him. I listen to some of his remarks. I did not have any personal contact with him. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the officer, high officer of SDA at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was a member of the parliament also, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he was not a member of the parliament. He was the Minister of the Interior. He was a member of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking to find out how he came to the parliament. On another occasion, while you were a member of the parliament, common room on their lobby, you have overheard the conversation where the Prijedor chapter of the SDS was criticised, who was the representative who criticised Prijedor chapter of SDS?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You said that the convention of the SDA was criticised --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prijedor SDS council.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I understand, I see now. The SDS party in Prijedor. Yes, I heard that in the breaks of the sessions in the assembly, sometimes those breaks were quite long and then we would sit down together and listen to the conversation --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a gentlemen from Pale; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was Mr. Ljubo Bosiljcic. He was the member of the parliament from the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you heard that criticism, you didn't know what that criticism was about, did you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew it, they told him that he wasn't doing his job properly, that he failed to achieve anything in Prijedor because they lost in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That that criticism was rendered because of the inefficient political organisation in Prijedor because they lost?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As for that criticism that we have been discussing now, it may have meant that. The reason could have been something else, some problems within the party, but I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, there were not any major problems between SDS and SDA until the war in Croatia broke out; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were problems regarding the allocation of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when, when the war in Croatia erupted, what was the position of SDA toward the draught, JNA draught, for Croatian war?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The SDA did not support the intervention of the JNA in Slovenia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you published any notices, any information, any positions as to the response to the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean at a local level in the Prijedor municipality? At the level of the republic, the political leaders stated their views and it was reported in the media. There was also discussion about that in the Bosnian parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, Bosnia and Herzegovina were a part of Yugoslavia, Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, were they?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, yes. That means several months after the new government was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: JNA was the official military of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at that time? I am talking July, August, September of '91.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but Yugoslavia had already been transformed and the status of the JNA --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am asking, I am asking is JNA at that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, yes, just a moment. We can only have one person speaking at a time. And, in this case, it was the witness. You must allow him to finish, Mr. Vucicevic. And then if you want to ask another question, do. Would you bear in mind also that everything has got to be interpreted, and therefore, there is a necessity for a discipline waiting before asking questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Was there anything you wanted to add, Mr. Semenovic, to that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to add that at the time this question referred to, there had already been democratic changes both in Slovenia and in Croatia. There were some changes in the Yugoslav leadership and Slovenia and Croatia passed certain legislation, which changed their status and their position within Yugoslavia. Our view was that, at that time, the peace process had already started, the process of negotiating on the transformation of Yugoslavia. Our view was that until a solution is found, first of all, that solution should be reached by peaceful means. But until such a solution is found, the army should not get involved in any conflicts in order to prevent a war breaking out. That was the view of the republican leadership and of the party. And, to that effect, we were opposed to the mobilisation because we deemed that negotiations should be conducted and not war. We shouldn't have a war of JNA against the people, the people that it was supposed to protect. That was the reason why it was established in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, when I simply asked you, and I still insist that you answer the question, if I may, please, Your Honour, is whether or not Bosnia was officially part of Yugoslavia in the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whether JNA was an army of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sometime in September of 1991, official army of the existing country of Yugoslavia, JNA, has issued a call for mobilisation in Prijedor area; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And having lived in that country for at least 20 or more years, re-service and active soldiers have responded to the call; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some did, some did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that most of the people who declared themselves as Bosniak Muslims did not respond to mobilisation call?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified last time when you were before the Trial Chamber, you said there were two units from Prijedor, 5th Kozara Brigade, which was to be 6th Krisca (Phon) Brigade beforehand and 343rd, later 43rd Brigade were filled up to their full formation by the re-service from Prijedor area; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not mention the 343 Brigade and the 43rd Brigade. I talked about the 5th, Kozara Brigade and the 6th Krajina Brigade. Because for a while, it had one name and for a while another. I don't remember which name was used at which time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, it's now five o'clock, is that a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll go on tomorrow. Mr. Semenovic, would you be back, please, tomorrow at half past nine. We have another matter to deal with, in fact, at nine o'clock, so I hope we'll be able to start this case at half past nine. But, if not, that is the reason. Could you be back tomorrow, please.
